answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the cedar schedule in the copper ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the vine checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 173 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. That is 35 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
